walkthroughs.body_html:
World Focus Music Study — a core area of GCSE Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

World Focus Music Study brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with World Focus Music Study.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: In Indian classical music, a tala is what?
options: A repeating cycle of beats
A plucked string instrument
A type of dance costume
A sliding ornament

mcqs.q: The gamelan tradition comes from which country?
options: Indonesia
Brazil
Egypt
Japan

mcqs.q: In an Indian classical performance, the tanpura provides what?
options: The drone
The main melody
The drum strokes
The lyrics
Several contrasting rhythms sounding at the same time
One rhythm played very loudly
A rhythm with no pulse
Everyone playing in unison

mcqs.q: Is a raga the same thing as a scale?
options: A raga is just the Indian word for a scale.
Only one drum is ever allowed to play at a time.
A raga is a kind of drum used in temples.
No - a raga includes a set of notes plus rules, characteristic phrases, ornaments and an associated mood, guiding improvisation.

mcqs.q: Do gamelan musicians play from written notation?
options: A raga is a kind of drum used in temples.
Traditionally they learn by ear and memory, internalising the cyclic structure and their part's relationship to the core melody.
Gamelan players read from staff notation like an orchestra.
Gamelan music is improvised freshly with no fixed pieces at all.

mcqs.q: Is African ensemble drumming an unstructured free-for-all?
options: No - each drum has a defined role within interlocking patterns, and a master drummer cues changes with signals.
Everyone just improvises loudly at once with no organisation.
Only one drum is ever allowed to play at a time.
Gamelan music is improvised freshly with no fixed pieces at all.
